subtopic: Dimensionality, Fact Tables and Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD)
question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #31: An executive revenue dashboard reported an overnight 200% discrepancy in Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) and Month-over-Month retention in BI Dashboards & Visual Analytics (PowerBI/Tableau/Metabase). Audit logs show data pipeline inaccuracies stemming from 'Dimensionality, Fact Tables and Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD)'.

### Engineering Challenge:
What is the correct analytical SQL and data modeling approach to ensure accurate metric aggregation for 'Dimensionality, Fact Tables and Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD)'?

options.text: Execute a CROSS JOIN between customer tables and raw event logs without deduplication.
Hardcode arbitrary multiplier factors into the reporting query to offset the calculated inflation.
Enforce distinct user-level keys in dimensional joins, isolate fan-out via CTE pre-aggregations, and utilize window framing (ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
Suppress all rows with duplicate dates by applying SELECT DISTINCT * across the entire warehouse.

answer_explanation: Metric distortion in BI Dashboards & Visual Analytics (PowerBI/Tableau/Metabase) typically arises from accidental Cartesian joins or improper window framing that multi-counts transactions when dimensional tables have multiple active rows. Pre-aggregating at the user/date grain before joining eliminates fan-out.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option C. Rationale: Metric distortion in BI Dashboards & Visual Analytics (PowerBI/Tableau/Metabase) typically arises from accidental Cartesian joins or improper window framing that multi-counts transactions when dimensional tables have multiple active rows. Pre-aggregating at the user/date grain before joining eliminates fan-out.
